descriptors.definition: A return of income is a formal declaration furnished by an assessee detailing total income, deductions, and tax payable in a prescribed format. Companies and firms must file it compulsorily, along with specific resident individuals holding foreign assets or signing authorities.
inclusion: Companies
Firms
Resident individuals holding foreign assets or financial interests
nearby_distinctions: Differs from a return of loss or revised return by being the primary mandatory periodic filing of taxable income under regular provisions.

descriptors.concept_name: Compulsory Filing Of Return Of Income [Section 139(1)]
descriptors.definition: Compulsory filing provisions mandate certain entities and individuals to submit a return of income on or before the due date regardless of income levels. This includes companies, firms, and residents holding foreign assets or signing authority, excluding certain beneficiaries whose income is included by the primary asset owner.
inclusion: Companies
Firms
Residents with foreign beneficial assets or signing powers
exclusion: Beneficiary whose asset income is already taxable in the hands of the beneficial owner
nearby_distinctions: Distinct from voluntary returns because statutory compliance is mandatory based on entity type or asset holding rather than income thresholds alone.

descriptors.concept_name: Interest For Default In Furnishing Return Of Income [Section 234A]
descriptors.definition: Interest under section 234A is levied when an assessee fails to furnish a return of income by the statutory due date. Simple interest at one percent per month applies to the net tax liability for the duration of the default period.
inclusion: Assessees filing returns after the due date
Assessees failing to furnish any return
exclusion: Assessees filing valid returns within the prescribed due date
nearby_distinctions: Calculated specifically on tax on total income reduced by advance tax and TDS, unlike late filing fees under section 234F.

descriptors.concept_name: Specified Class Or Classes Of Persons To Be Exempted From Filing Return Of Income [Section 139(1C)]
descriptors.definition: The Central Government may exempt specific classes of taxpayers from filing a return of income to minimize compliance burdens. This includes non-corporate non-residents and foreign companies whose sole Indian income derives from specified International Financial Services Centre investment funds subject to tax deduction at source.
inclusion: Non-corporate non-residents with fund income in IFSC
Foreign companies with fund income in IFSC
exclusion: Taxpayers earning other Indian-sourced incomes outside the specified exemptions
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from standard filing requirements by granting total exemption from submitting returns under section 139(1) via executive notification.

descriptors.definition: A return of loss must be filed within the normal due dates to enable the carry forward and set-off of specified business, capital, or specific activity losses. Failure to file this return on time forfeits the right to carry forward those specific categories of losses.
inclusion: Business losses
Speculation losses
Capital losses
exclusion: House property losses and unabsorbed depreciation which can be carried forward even without timely filing
nearby_distinctions: Mandatory filing is strictly required for business and capital losses, unlike house property losses which tolerate delayed filings for carry forward purposes.

descriptors.definition: A belated return is filed by any person who missed the original due date, submitted prior to three months before the end of the assessment year or before assessment completion. Filing a belated return incurs interest, late fees, and restrictions on carrying forward certain losses or claiming specific deductions.
inclusion: Returns submitted after the section 139(1) due date within permitted statutory windows
exclusion: Returns filed after the expiry of the belated filing deadline
nearby_distinctions: Unlike original timely returns, belated returns restrict loss carry-forward privileges and strip eligibility for specific tax incentive deductions.

descriptors.concept_name: Return Of Income Of Charitable Trusts And Institutions [Section 139(4A)]
descriptors.definition: Every person in receipt of income held under a trust for charitable or religious purposes must furnish a return of income if total income before exemptions exceeds the basic exemption limit. Representative assessees must file these returns voluntarily within prescribed timelines.
inclusion: Trusts holding property for charitable or religious obligations
Institutions receiving voluntary contributions
exclusion: Trusts whose gross income before exemptions stays at or below the basic exemption limit
nearby_distinctions: Differs from individual returns by computing income thresholds prior to applying statutory charitable exemptions under sections 11 and 12.

descriptors.concept_name: Return Of Income Of Political Parties [Section 139(4B)]
descriptors.definition: The chief executive officer of a political party must file a return of income if the party's total income before specific exemptions exceeds the basic exemption limit. Submitting this return and completing mandatory audits are prerequisites for claiming tax exemptions.
inclusion: Political parties exceeding the basic exemption limit prior to exemptions
exclusion: Political parties with total income below the basic exemption threshold
nearby_distinctions: Conditioned strictly on mandatory audit requirements to secure tax exemptions unavailable to generic non-compliant associations.

descriptors.concept_name: Mandatory Filing Of Returns By Research Associations, News Agency, Trade Unions, Etc. [Section 139(4C)]
descriptors.definition: Specific specialized entities such as research associations, news agencies, and trade unions are statutorily required to file returns of income if their total income, before factoring in specific statutory exemptions, exceeds the basic exemption limit. These returns follow the procedural parameters applicable to standard corporate filings.
inclusion: Research associations
Mutual funds
Trade unions exceeding basic exemption limits
exclusion: Entities falling below the basic exemption limit prior to exemptions
nearby_distinctions: Applies to an exhaustive list of specialized statutory entities whose exemption claims are contingent upon threshold-based return filings.

descriptors.concept_name: Mandatory Filing Of Returns By Universities, Colleges Etc. [Section 139(4D)]
descriptors.definition: Universities, colleges, and specified scientific research institutions not otherwise mandated under other return provisions must file an annual return of income or loss. All operational provisions governing standard income returns apply directly to these educational institutions.
inclusion: Universities and colleges referred in section 35(1)
Institutions lacking other return obligations
exclusion: Institutions already required to file under alternative provisions of section 139
nearby_distinctions: Focuses exclusively on educational and research institutions specified under scientific research provisions rather than general commercial entities.

descriptors.concept_name: Filing Of Return Of Income By A Business Trust [Section 139(4E)]
descriptors.definition: Every business trust must furnish a return of its income or loss for every previous year if it has no separate filing mandate under other subsections. Standard procedural rules and provisions applicable to regular income returns govern these business trusts.
inclusion: All business trusts not otherwise filing under alternative provisions
exclusion: Business trusts covered under separate compulsory clauses
nearby_distinctions: Imposes universal annual filing obligations specifically tailored to business trust structures regardless of income performance.

descriptors.concept_name: Filing Of Return Of Income By Investment Fund Section 139(4F)]
descriptors.definition: Investment funds defined under specific statutory pass-through provisions must furnish an annual return of income or loss for every previous year. General tax provisions regulate these submissions as if they were standard returns filed under primary provisions.
inclusion: Investment funds referred to in section 115UB
exclusion: Funds already filing under alternative statutory sub-sections
nearby_distinctions: Specifically targets specialized investment funds governed by pass-through taxation mechanics rather than standard corporate entities.
